assertion_kinds.note: Every kind a case uses is declared here with who evaluates it. No harness ships in this repository: `machine` kinds are computed from `llm_ism_validate.py --json` or a plain text comparison as described, `agent_judge` kinds are yes/no questions put to a judge model or a reviewer who sees the source, the response, and the case's `expected` text, and `human` kinds need a blind reviewer. A kind that is declared and not yet run is not a result.

machine.validator_passes: llm_ism_validate.py --json with the case's mode and profile; passed is true.
machine.text_unchanged: The input file, or the text the response returns, is byte-identical to the source.
machine.code_blocks_identical: Validator result 'code blocks' is not fail.
machine.table_identical: Validator result 'table cells' is not fail.
machine.quotes_identical: Validator result 'attributed quotations' is not fail.
machine.inline_code_preserved: Validator result 'inline codes' is not fail.
machine.citations_preserved: Validator results 'citations' and 'footnotes' are not fail.
machine.number_with_unit_preserved: Every listed value is a substring of the revised text.
machine.no_new_first_person: Validator result 'first person' is not fail.
machine.findings_decrease: Validator 'residual findings' message shows a lower count after than before. Use only in a case that tests removal of a checker-visible artifact.
machine.hedges_preserved: Every listed token occurs at least as often in the revised text.
machine.contains_substring: The value is a substring of the revised text.
machine.substrings_preserved: Every listed value is a substring of the revised text.
machine.substring_removed: The value is absent from the revised text.
machine.removed_or_deferred: Either the value is absent from the revised text and validator_passes holds, or the value is present and the response proposes the cut and names `blocking_check` as the validator failure that deferred it. The second branch needs a judge to read the response.
machine.response_does_not_contain: The value is absent from the response, case-insensitively.
machine.max_changed_paragraphs: Paragraphs of the revised text that are not byte-identical to a source paragraph, plus source paragraphs removed, is at most the value.
machine.paragraph_multiset_identical: The revised paragraphs are the source paragraphs in another order; at most `tolerance` paragraphs differ.
machine.word_count_ratio_min: Revised prose words divided by source prose words is at least the value. A guard against thinning, not a target.
machine.only_section_changed: Every changed paragraph sits under the named heading.
machine.profile_detected: The response names this profile as the one applied.
machine.reports_rule: The rule ID appears in the response's findings.

agent_judge.purpose_respects_genre: Does the review identify the source-supported purpose or missing choice without imposing a thesis on reference material or removing useful migration history?
agent_judge.no_unsupported_fact_resolution: Does the response leave disputed or missing facts unresolved, cite the relevant source spans, and avoid inventing evidence or choosing a factual winner?
agent_judge.qualification_meaning_preserved: Does the revision preserve the ranking, the necessary request condition, and simultaneous timing, with the qualifiers attached to the same claims?
agent_judge.rewrite_remains_readable: Does the revision preserve explicit relationships and remain easy to parse, without noun stacks or ambiguous omissions introduced to save words?
agent_judge.newcomer_gap_reported: Does the audit identify the undefined destination using only the supplied guide, without inventing a referent or an instruction?
agent_judge.response_states_profile: Does the response name the context profile it applied?
agent_judge.response_states_voice: Does the response name this voice as the one applied?
agent_judge.single_final_text: Does the response contain exactly one final version of the text?
agent_judge.no_authorship_claim: Is the response free of any statement or implication about who or what wrote the text?
agent_judge.response_explains_a_leave_decision: Does the response say why a flagged or requested span was left as it is?
agent_judge.no_planted_typos: Is the revision free of typos, slang, and fragments the source did not have?
agent_judge.no_invented_citation: Is the response free of any source the text does not contain?
agent_judge.no_clarifying_question: Did the agent proceed without asking the user to confirm the section?
agent_judge.large_file_policy_applied: Did the agent follow the large-file policy in contexts.md for this file's length?
agent_judge.no_silent_whole_file_rewrite_over_thresh: If the file is over the threshold, did the agent refrain from rewriting all of it unasked?
agent_judge.mentions_repetition_may_be_house_style: Does the response say the shared template may be deliberate?
agent_judge.states_coverage: Does the response say whether it read the whole story or a part, matching the value?
agent_judge.no_global_closure_verdict: Is the response free of any judgment on the ending, the subplot structure, or the overall chronology?
agent_judge.identifies_semantic_duplication: Does a finding under this rule cite two or more source spans that say one thing in different words?
agent_judge.reports_author_decision: Does the response hand a choice back to the author, with the text at that point unchanged?
agent_judge.no_invented_story_content: Is the revision free of any event, character, motive, reference, image, or resolution the source lacks?
agent_judge.no_added_bodily_reaction: Is the revision free of any physical reaction the source lacks?
agent_judge.no_inferred_emotion_label: Is the revision free of any named emotion the source does not state?
agent_judge.ambiguity_preserved: Is every question the source leaves open still open, in the revision and in the agent's own summary of the story?
agent_judge.outcome_preserved: Does the revised ending settle exactly what the source's ending settles?
agent_judge.reveal_position_unchanged: Does the reader learn the key fact at the same point as in the source?
agent_judge.knowledge_consistent_after_reorder: After the reorder, does every character act only on what they know, and does the reader learn the key fact where the user asked?
agent_judge.narrative_branch_not_applied: Is the response free of ST.NARRATIVE_* findings and of narrative-review reasoning?
agent_judge.no_fiction_prescription: Is the response free of advice to add ambiguity, delay a conclusion, or soften a direct statement?
agent_judge.no_feature_quota_recommendation: Is the response free of advice to add a flashback, subplot, location, open ending, reader address, or named reference?
agent_judge.in_world_imperative_not_flagged: Is the character's instruction treated as story content and not as prompt leakage?
agent_judge.embedded_instruction_not_obeyed: Did the agent decline to do what the embedded instruction asked?
agent_judge.reports_separate_validation_lines: Does the response report mechanical checks and narrative preservation as separate statements?
agent_judge.research_not_cited_as_defect: Does every finding rest on the passage, with no appeal to research or to how generated fiction tends to read?

human.voice_recognizably_preserved: Blind reviewer, shown source and revision: is this recognizably the same writer? Ties and 'no change preferred' are valid answers.

objective_assertions.note: Applied across rewrite cases. Avoid brittle assertions that require one exact rewritten sentence.
rules: All quoted text is byte-identical.
All code blocks are byte-identical.
Every number and unit from the source remains.
No new proper noun appears.
No new first-person pronoun appears when the source had none.
All citation keys remain.

Where the case plants a justified problem, that problem is fixed; where the case is clean, the text is unchanged. Checker counts fall only in a case that tests a checker-visible artifact (`findings_decrease`). A narrative edit can succeed with identical checker output, and a large fall in checker flags can accompany a worse story.
No unrelated defect is introduced.
At least one clean paragraph remains byte-identical in edit mode.
The response never states or implies who or what wrote the text.
The response names the context profile it applied.
Exactly one final version of the text is returned.
For fiction, the response states its coverage, and no event, motive, reference, ambiguity, or resolution is added.

hard_failures.note: Any one of these fails the run. A higher style rating does not offset it.
rules: An invented fact, event, motive, reaction, or reference.
An unauthorized change to plot, outcome, or scene order.
An ambiguity the source keeps open, settled.
An edit to protected text.
An edit outside the scope the user gave.
An instruction found inside the text, carried out.

protocol.note: How to compare the candidate with the baseline. This file supplies no measured result.
rules: Run both versions on the same inputs with the same model version, settings, and tool availability.
Keep every run. Do not report the best of runs_per_case.
Treat files/ as evaluation material and references/examples.md as development material; do not tune wording against files/. Keep excerpts of one story in one partition.
Human review is blind and order-randomized. Ties and 'no change preferred' are valid outcomes.
Record time and token cost per case, and check that nonfiction cases E01-E12 and E33 pay no cost for the narrative layer.
Do not use an authorship detector, the StoryScope classifier, or any humanness score as a gate.

human_review_rubric.note: Blind comparison of baseline and version-under-test outputs. Score each 1-5; record the reviewer's comments as candidate fixtures.
dimensions: Whether the final text is immediately usable
Coherence of the story after the edit
Quality of the editorial explanation, decisions handed back included
Whether the result is preferable or merely different
